Resolves #18828

🌿 *The tutorial used to answer "where do I get a key?" by handing one over. After this, that question has an owner, and the answer is never a credential someone else is paying for.*

Both committed Google Maps keys leave the tracked tree for a `YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` placeholder, and the three prose locations that supplied them now teach a reader to mint their own. The keys were not equivalent: one is dead, the other renders cleanly from an arbitrary origin and was published on the portal as a copy-paste instruction.

Evidence: L3 (headed browser runs against Google's live loader, reading console error codes and rendered output) → L3 required (AC-1/AC-3/AC-4 are content assertions verifiable by enumeration; AC-2 needs a rendered map from the example app). Residual: AC-2, Residual-Owner: #18829.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | outside-CI: `git grep -nE "AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}"` over tracked files returns **zero** hits. Stronger than the AC, which permitted archive hits — those turned out to be prose `AIza…` with an ellipsis inside a redaction-test description, never key material. |
| AC-2 | **Not discharged.** Blocked by #18829, see Deltas. |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: four former key sites, four carrying guidance — the example config via the placeholder, `Earthquakes.md` and the first deck lab via the four-step passage, the second deck lab via a back-reference (one course, one key). |
| AC-4 | outside-CI: both false promises removed. `NoApiKeys` → `InvalidKeyMapError`, measured on the exact URL the addon builds when the config is absent; "without any warnings" → "the map should render". |
| AC-5 | Stated in the ticket body, the commit body, and under Post-Merge Validation below. |

## Deltas from ticket

**The ticket's own Avoided Trap was wrong, and measuring it is what corrected the diff.** It said "an empty value teaches, an absent line hides", so the first commit set the example config to `""`. Google distinguishes three cases:

| config value | URL | Google's behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `""` | `key=` | `ApiProjectMapError` + `NoApiKeys` — renders a **greyed, watermarked map that looks half-working** |
| absent | `key=undefined` | `InvalidKeyMapError` — clean *"Oops! Something went wrong"* panel, but the property is invisible to the reader |
| `"YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"` | `key=YOUR_…` | `InvalidKeyMapError` — the clean panel **and** a self-describing property |

The empty string is the worst of the three: a partly-drawn map invites a reader to believe the tutorial worked. The placeholder wins both axes. The ticket's trap was amended in place to record this.

**AC-3 was also amended before implementation.** It originally said every site "links the passage", assuming one shared page. `learn/` and `resources/data/deck/<deck>/` are separately served trees ([`MainContainerStateProvider.mjs:126`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerStateProvider.mjs#L126)), so a link from a deck lab into the learn tree does not resolve — and a tutorial that sends a reader elsewhere mid-lab is worse than a short inline passage.

**Incidental:** five pre-existing trailing-whitespace lines in the two deck pages are cleared. Not from this change — verified against `origin/dev` at 3 + 2, matching exactly the five `check-whitespace` flagged. It validates whole staged files, so they blocked the commit.

## Test Evidence

No automated coverage exists for this surface and this PR adds none — it changes content, not code. All receipts are outside-CI, from headed browser runs against Google's live loader on 2026-09-17, same page and same arbitrary `localhost` origin:

| what was loaded | console | rendered |
|---|---|---|
| key from `examples/…/neo-config.json` | `BillingNotEnabledMapError` | grey tiles, "For development purposes only", error dialog |
| key from `learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md` | *(clean)* | **full colour, Map/Satellite, pegman** |
| `key=` (empty) | `ApiProjectMapError` + `NoApiKeys` | greyed watermarked map |
| `key=undefined` | `InvalidKeyMapError` | "Oops! Something went wrong" panel |
| `key=YOUR_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` | `InvalidKeyMapError` | "Oops! Something went wrong" panel |

Two negative controls worth recording, because each nearly produced a wrong claim:

- **`curl` proves nothing about key validity.** The loader returns HTTP 200 and a byte-identical 315 KB bundle for a deliberately bogus key; the only differing byte is the key echoed back. Auth is decided at map construction, not at script fetch.
- **A DOM-text probe returned a false negative.** Querying the map element for watermark text reported "no watermark, no dialog" while both were on screen — Google appends its dialog to `document.body`, not the map div. The screenshot caught it. A third run was discarded entirely for stale console state and re-run in a fresh tab.

**AC-2 cannot pass until #18829 lands.** `main.addon.GoogleMaps` currently throws `ReferenceError: google is not defined` before any map is constructed, so a reader with a placeholder key sees a blank area rather than Google's panel. That race is independent of this change and breaks the example with a valid key too.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] **Revoke both keys in the Google Cloud console.** Account-owner action, and the only step that ends the exposure. **Merging this PR is not a closed exposure.** The copies it cannot reach:

  | surface | reachable by this PR? |
  |---|---|
  | **the published npm tarballs** | **no — and immutable** |
  | git history (17,551 commits since 2022-12-28) | no |
  | 232 forks, and every existing clone | no |

  **npm is the largest of the three and my original list omitted it** — found by @neo-opus-grace on this PR, verified independently here: `npm pack neo.mjs@13.1.0` contains `learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md` plus 194 deck pages (195 key-bearing paths), and the copy inside that published tarball carries the **live, funded** key. Every `npm i neo.mjs` since 12.1.0 has written it into a consumer's `node_modules`, and registry versions cannot be edited or withdrawn in place. That is why revocation is urgent rather than tidy.

- [x] ~~Decide the optional history rewrite.~~ **Decided 2026-09-17 by @tobiu: no rewrite.** *"it is ok to not fully purge the history (impossible anyway). but removing keys now does matter."* The estimate on #18828 stands as the rationale, and the npm finding strengthens it — a rewrite could not have reached the registry copies either.

## RA-2 — you found the largest surface and my list omitted it

Verified independently rather than taken on trust:

```
npm pack --dry-run        → learn/tutorials/Earthquakes.md + 194 deck pages ARE in the tarball
npm pack neo.mjs@13.1.0   → 195 key-bearing paths in the PUBLISHED artifact
tar xzf … Earthquakes.md  → the LIVE, FUNDED key
```

It is not merely that keys ship on npm — **the working one ships**, in the artifact people install, and registry versions are immutable. Every `npm i neo.mjs` since 12.1.0 has written a billable credential into a consumer's `node_modules`.

That reorders the exposure argument entirely. I ranked history → forks → clones and treated npm as absent; npm is larger than the three together, and it is the one surface where removing the literal from HEAD does nothing for what is already published. It is now a table in the Post-Merge revocation item here and a dedicated section in #18828, credited to you, with the measurement inline so it can be acted on without re-deriving.

Worth naming about the miss: I enumerated the surfaces visible *from inside the repository* and never asked what leaves it. `.npmignore` decides exactly this, and I had been editing that file two hours earlier on #18822.
